# typed-sql 2.1.0

typed-sql 2.1 makes repeated typed SQL fragments a first-class query-building primitive, completes
the grammar-owned PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite analysis paths, and promotes SQLite to the stable
release train. Unsupported or incomplete language forms continue to fail closed.

## Highlights

- Non-empty arrays of typed fragments can be interpolated directly as homogeneous, comma-separated
  SQL structure. This supports type-safe multi-row inserts built with `items.map(...)` without an
  explicit join helper, while ordinary arrays remain single bound values.
- PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite now own their parsers, ASTs, tokenization, walking, versioned
  built-in catalogs, capability selection, and diagnostics. The historical multi-dialect parser is
  retained only as a deprecated typed-sql 2.x compatibility surface.
- Schema snapshot format 2 adds canonical relation, constraint, index, type, routine, server-version,
  and capability evidence. Version 1 and version 2 codecs remain isolated, with conservative v1
  upgrades for existing projects.
- PostgreSQL analysis expands across supported majors 14 through 18 with complete DML, compound and
  recursive queries, advanced query structure, SQL/JSON forms, operator and cast selection,
  extension manifests, introspection, and hardened execution behavior.
- MySQL analysis adds mode-aware lexical behavior, complete DML and query structure, versioned
  catalogs and support policy, schema-v2 introspection, collation-aware resolution, and hardened
  runtime protocol handling.
- SQLite is now stable, with versioned JSON, JSONB, date/time, math, and extension catalogs; complete
  schema-v2 evidence; and an optional hardened `node:sqlite` adapter.
- The published conformance v2 API adds feature-addressable static and live differential testing,
  exact-claim enforcement, reproduction evidence, and version-aware grammar feature ledgers.
- A shared, versioned source-analysis service and `typed-sql doctor` provide deterministic compiler,
  schema, grammar, capability, and editor compatibility identities with privacy-safe diagnostics.

## Upgrade and compatibility

Read the [v1 to v2 upgrade contract](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/upgrading-from-v1)
when upgrading an older grammar, schema snapshot, or custom adapter. The
[compatibility reference](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility) records the
supported and exactly tested environments.

The stable packages support Node.js 22.11 or newer. The compiler correctness path uses TypeScript
7.0.2. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are stable dialect packages. PostgreSQL and MySQL use
application-installed drivers; SQLite's optional built-in adapter supports Node 22.13+, 24, and 26.

The following packages publish on the stable train:

- `@typed-sql/core`
- `@typed-sql/opentelemetry`
- `@typed-sql/ast`
- `@typed-sql/schema`
- `@typed-sql/config`
- `@typed-sql/compiler`
- `@typed-sql/conformance`
- `@typed-sql/postgres`
- `@typed-sql/mysql`
- `@typed-sql/sqlite`
- `@typed-sql/cli`

`@typed-sql/ts-bridge`, `@typed-sql/language-server`, and the editor integrations remain
experimental. They stay on the `next` npm tag and are not dependencies of the stable packages. The
preview TypeScript and editor integration remains isolated from the stable compiler path.

## Evidence

The protected release workflow verifies the exact release commit, exercises real packed-consumer
PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite environments, packs and installs the eleven-package stable train, and
accepts the published release candidate from npm before promotion. Publication is retry-safe and
verifies the stable packages from npm before creating these aggregate release notes.
